messages.subject: Re: undocumented Subread behavior
messages.body_plain:
Subread aligner uses a lot of parameters to control its sensitivity and specificity in mapping reads and detecting genomic variants. We only made some of these parameters be tunable by users to ease the use of our program and our documentation is provided for these parameters only.

We have released version 1.4.6-p2 on Mar 24 and a new parameter called "--minDistanceBetweenVariants" was added to allow users to specify the minimum required distance between neighbouring variants. We found that allowing a very small distance may greatly increase the running time of the alignment and therefore we decided to allow users to tune this parameter to suit different needs.

We apologize if this parameter has caused any problems to your projects. Every aligner uses a lot of parameters and usually only part of the parameters are documented. I hope you find that our documentation for Subread aligner is better than many other software programs, but it is certainly our intention to make it more complete and accurate.

Thank you for using Subread and we look forward to having more comments/suggestions from you.

Wei

messages.subject: Observed inability to follow symlinks for featureCounts
messages.subject_clean: Observed inability to follow symlinks for featureCounts
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have observed that featureCounts has problems following symlinks :-( I have a few hundred pairs of BAM/BAI files, classified according to source and tissue type and to simplify my analysis pipeline, I created symlinks to the originals in a single folder, with recoded names for reading.  When I try featureCounts with the original file, it runs a-ok, telling me that it detected a BAM file; however if I try using the symlink, it fails by telling me that it failed to open the file and labelling it an unknown file. However, if I try both paths with samtools flagstat, no problems are observed: both provides the expected results. This tells me that featureCounts does not resolve symlinks. Is that the case? If it is, is there a flag to add to tell it to do so?

Thanks in advance

S. Foisy
Project Manager
Bioinformatics
Montreal Heart Institute
Montreal, Qc

messages.subject: featureCounts returns exit code zero when given bad annotation file
messages.subject_clean: featureCounts returns exit code zero when given bad annotation file
messages.body_plain:
Hi Wei,

When I submit jobs to my HPC, I check the exit codes after they run. Based on the exit code, I log whether the job was a success or failure. I thought I had successfully run a bunch of featureCounts jobs this morning, but it turns out the jobs failed but still returned exit code 0. The error was that the annotation file was bad (I had moved the annotation file but not updated the symlink to point to the new location).

Normally when I give featureCounts bad input, it properly exits with an error code, e.g.

$ featureCounts nonsense 2> /dev/null
$ echo $?
255

However, when I give it a bad annotation file, it returns exit code 0.

$ featureCounts -a nonsense -F SAF -o output bam/19098.1.A01.ATTAGACG.L002.R1.C6WYKACXX.trim.bam 2> error.txt
$ echo $?
0
$ tail -n 2 error.txt
|| Load annotation file nonsense ...                                          ||
Failed to open the annotation file nonsense, or its format is incorrect, or it contains no 'exon' features.

Why does featureCounts return 0 when there it encounters an error?

Thanks,

John
